Tutoring, become a student assistant, anything off campus that wouldn't interfere with your studies.

The main thing you should avoid is anything interfering with your classes.

If you are scientifically inclined, you could always clean test tunes in a lab. Hook yourself up to a researcher and do the free apprentice thing.

Alternatively, if you are into the arts, get yourself a camera and shoot porn. It will make you some money and expand your social circle considerably.

Intern. Pays the bills, and it's fantastic work experience for after you graduate. The only caveat is that if you're in a, shall we say, "fluffy" field, it may not be as well paid as e.g. a STEM internship.

STEM: get into a lab that does research.

Everything Else: bartend and make money.
Campus jobs are always really convenient. Being a cashier or a cook at a dining hall isn't that bad, nor is being a hall advisor / front desk worker. If you can land a research position, even better.

If your program is at all expensive/rigorous, focus on that. You're unlikely to make enough money part time to be worth missing the investment you've already made in paying that tuition.

And it's not all about classes—networking with the students and professors is important too.

Now if you can get paid to do something that will directly further your career/studies, that's a win/win and by all means go for it.

Being an RA is a sweet gig if you have the right people on your floor. A lot of colleges will give you free room, a partial meal plan and stipend money. A bunch of my friends did it for Juniors and Seniors (21+ so alcohol wasn't a violation) and they said it was awesome. It also shows future employers that you are responsible.
